skill.name: yescan-ocr-universal
skill.description: Use this skill to extract, recognize, and structure text from images, screenshots, photos, and scanned documents. It supports handwriting, tables, formulas, IDs, invoices, tickets, licenses, medical reports, product labels, and image translation through the Quark Scan King OCR service.
skill.summary: Extract structured text from images across 19 OCR scenes using Quark Scan King.
skill.author: yescan-ai

security_audit.summary: The skill is an OCR client that sends user images and SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY to the Quark Scan King service and can write translated images to /tmp/imgs. Confirmed risks include outbound sensitive document transfer, plaintext hidden API-key storage, temporary output files, and secret handling; most command execution, Windows Credential Manager, obfuscation, and high-entropy alerts are false positives from markdown or ordinary image/Base64 handling. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Sensitive images are sent to a third-party OCR service.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit user consent guidance for IDs, medical records, and financial documents, and document retention, region, and compliance terms before processing.

remediation.issue: API keys may be stored in plaintext at ~/.yescan_env.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer platform secret storage or environment variables, and keep file fallback optional with strict permissions and rotation guidance.

remediation.issue: Translated images are written to temporary storage without automatic cleanup.
remediation.suggestion: Add a cleanup option, document deletion steps, and consider a user-selected output directory with restrictive permissions.

remediation.issue: URL input accepts arbitrary http and https destinations.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and block loopback, private, link-local, and cloud metadata address ranges before forwarding URLs to the OCR service.

remediation.issue: Documentation says the API key is sent in a header while code sends aiApiKey in the JSON body.
remediation.suggestion: Align documentation with the actual transport path or update the client to use a provider-supported header if available.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Document Images Sent to Third-Party OCR Service
semantic_findings.description: The skill explicitly supports IDs, social security cards, travel permits, degree certificates, tickets, invoices, medical reports, and other sensitive documents. The privacy documentation states user-provided images are sent to scan-business.quark.cn for OCR, so sensitive personal or regulated data leaves the user environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The supported scenes include multiple PII and medical document types, and the privacy table confirms image data is transmitted to a third-party OCR service.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Transport Documentation Mismatch
semantic_findings.description: The privacy and security documents describe SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY as sent in an HTTP header. The implementation instead places the key in the JSON request body as aiApiKey, which weakens auditability and may mislead users reviewing exposure paths.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation says the key is sent as a header, while the request builder clearly includes aiApiKey inside the JSON payload.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary URL Forwarding Without Private Address Filtering
semantic_findings.description: The URL validator accepts any http or https URL and does not block private, loopback, or metadata addresses before forwarding dataUrl to the OCR service. If the upstream service fetches supplied URLs, this can enable abuse of the provider as a URL fetcher.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The local validator only checks scheme and parseability, then the client forwards the URL as dataUrl. Impact depends on upstream fetch behavior, so confidence is high enough to retain but not maximal.

content.user_title: Extract Text from Images with OCR
content.value_statement: Images and scanned documents often contain text that is hard to reuse. This skill sends one image to an OCR service and returns structured text for the matching document type.
actual_capabilities: Accepts one image URL, local image path, or Base64 image input.
Routes requests across 19 OCR scenes, including IDs, invoices, tickets, tables, formulas, and general text.
Returns structured OCR fields from the Quark Scan King API response.
Extracts handwriting, printed text, product label text, and medical or inspection report fields.
Creates a translated image file for the pic-translate scene and returns its local path.
limitations: Requires Python 3.9, network access, and a configured SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY.
Sends image content and the API key to a third-party OCR service.
Processes one image per run and does not support video or batch processing.
Local image inputs must be 5 MB or smaller and use a supported image format.

use_cases.title: Digitize Business Documents
use_cases.description: Extract key fields from invoices, business licenses, tickets, and forms for faster record entry.

use_cases.title: Process Finance Evidence
use_cases.description: Read VAT invoices, train tickets, and commercial invoices before reimbursement or audit review.

use_cases.title: Convert Study Materials
use_cases.description: Recognize formulas, questions, tables, and handwritten notes from classroom or research images.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Basic Text
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner OCR for a single image file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the text from this image: /path/to/image.png

prompt_templates.title: Read an Invoice
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate extraction from a known business document type.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this invoice image and return the seller, buyer, date, line items, tax amount, and total: /path/to/invoice.jpg

prompt_templates.title: Recognize a Table
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured extraction from a table screenshot.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the table from this screenshot and keep the row and column structure: /path/to/table.png

prompt_templates.title: Classify and Extract
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow when the document type is not known in advance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify the best OCR scene for this document, extract the key fields, and preserve important labels: /path/to/document.webp

output_examples.input: A photo of a VAT invoice.
output: Invoice type, invoice number, issue date, seller, buyer, tax amount, and total are returned as structured fields.
The result can be copied into a finance review workflow.
Rows, columns, and cell text are returned in a table-like structure.
Merged or unclear cells may need manual review.

output_examples.input: A foreign-language menu image for translation.
output: Recognized text and translated text are returned.
A translated image is saved locally and its path is returned.

best_practices: Confirm that users approve third-party OCR processing before sending sensitive images.
Use environment variables or a protected secret store for the API key when possible.
Delete temporary translated image files when they are no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Do not process government IDs, medical reports, or financial records without a clear compliance basis.
Do not pass a directory path or ask the skill to scan many files in one run.
Do not paste API keys into prompts, command arguments, screenshots, or shared logs.

faq.question: Does this skill work without an API key?
faq.answer: No. It requires SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY for the Quark Scan King service.

faq.question: Can it process local image files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can read one user-specified local image path and send the image content for OCR.

faq.question: Where is image data sent?
faq.answer: The skill sends image input to scan-business.quark.cn for OCR processing.

faq.question: Does it support scanned tables?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the table OCR scene when the image contains a table that should keep row and column structure.

faq.question: Can it translate text inside an image?
faq.answer: Yes. The pic-translate scene returns translated text and saves a translated image locally.

faq.question: Does it handle multiple images at once?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow processes one image per invocation.
